claim: Cullin-3 (CUL3)-based ubiquitin ligases regulate endosome maturation and trafficking of endocytic cargo to lysosomes in mammalian cells.
source: Cullin-3 (CUL3)-based ubiquitin ligases regulate endosome maturation and trafficking of endocytic cargo to lysosomes in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: CUL3-based ubiquitin ligase functions depend on SPOPL, a substrate-specific CUL3 adaptor.
source: Here, we report that these functions depend on SPOPL, a substrate-specific CUL3 adaptor.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: SPOPL associates with endosomes.
source: We find that SPOPL associates with endosomes and is required for both the formation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) and the endocytic host cell entry of influenza A virus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: SPOPL is required for the formation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs).
source: We find that SPOPL associates with endosomes and is required for both the formation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) and the endocytic host cell entry of influenza A virus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: SPOPL is required for the endocytic host cell entry of influenza A virus.
source: We find that SPOPL associates with endosomes and is required for both the formation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) and the endocytic host cell entry of influenza A virus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: In SPOPL-depleted cells, endosomes are enlarged and fail to acquire intraluminal vesicles (ILVs).
source: In SPOPL-depleted cells, endosomes are enlarged and fail to acquire intraluminal vesicles (ILVs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by microscopy data.

claim: EPS15 is a critical substrate ubiquitinated by CUL3-SPOPL.
source: We identify a critical substrate ubiquitinated by CUL3-SPOPL as EPS15, an endocytic adaptor that also associates with the ESCRT-0 complex members HRS and STAM on endosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: EPS15 is an endocytic adaptor that associates with the ESCRT-0 complex members HRS and STAM on endosomes.
source: We identify a critical substrate ubiquitinated by CUL3-SPOPL as EPS15, an endocytic adaptor that also associates with the ESCRT-0 complex members HRS and STAM on endosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: EPS15 is ubiquitinated in a SPOPL-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, EPS15 is ubiquitinated in a SPOPL-dependent manner, and accumulates with HRS in cells lacking SPOPL.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: EPS15 accumulates with HRS in cells lacking SPOPL.
source: Indeed, EPS15 is ubiquitinated in a SPOPL-dependent manner, and accumulates with HRS in cells lacking SPOPL.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: A CUL3-SPOPL E3 ubiquitin ligase complex regulates endocytic trafficking and MVB formation by ubiquitinating and degrading EPS15 at endosomes.
source: Together, our data indicates that a CUL3-SPOPL E3 ubiquitin ligase complex regulates endocytic trafficking and MVB formation by ubiquitinating and degrading EPS15 at endosomes, thereby influencing influenza A virus infection as well as degradation of EGFR and other EPS15 targets.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: CUL3-SPOPL-mediated regulation of EPS15 influences influenza A virus infection.
source: Together, our data indicates that a CUL3-SPOPL E3 ubiquitin ligase complex regulates endocytic trafficking and MVB formation by ubiquitinating and degrading EPS15 at endosomes, thereby influencing influenza A virus infection as well as degradation of EGFR and other EPS15 targets.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the data.

claim: CUL3-SPOPL-mediated regulation of EPS15 influences degradation of EGFR and other EPS15 targets.
source: Together, our data indicates that a CUL3-SPOPL E3 ubiquitin ligase complex regulates endocytic trafficking and MVB formation by ubiquitinating and degrading EPS15 at endosomes, thereby influencing influenza A virus infection as well as degradation of EGFR and other EPS15 targets.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Endocytic trafficking is an essential cellular process for nutrition absorption, signal transduction, cell-cell communication and maintenance of cell homeostasis.
source: Endocytic trafficking is an essential cellular process for nutrition absorption, signal transduction, cell-cell communication and maintenance of cell homeostasis (Doherty and McMahon, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Endocytosis is used for the uptake of exogenous and cellular cargo, including many viruses such as influenza A virus (IAV).
source: Endocytosis is used for the uptake of exogenous and cellular cargo, including many viruses such as influenza A virus (IAV) (Cossart and Helenius, 2014; Edinger et al., 2014) or a cohort of plasma membrane proteins such as the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with their respective ligands (Tomas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Endocytosis is used for the uptake of plasma membrane proteins such as the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with their respective ligands.
source: Endocytosis is used for the uptake of exogenous and cellular cargo, including many viruses such as influenza A virus (IAV) (Cossart and Helenius, 2014; Edinger et al., 2014) or a cohort of plasma membrane proteins such as the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with their respective ligands (Tomas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Cargo entering the endosomal system can be delivered via early (EE) and late endosomes (LE) to lysosomes (LY) for degradation, or alternatively, recycled back to the plasma membrane.
source: Cargo entering the endosomal system can be delivered via early (EE) and late endosomes (LE) to lysosomes (LY) for degradation, or alternatively, recycled back to the plasma membrane (Maxfield, 2014; Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Transfer of cargo from EEs to LYs depends on an endosomal maturation process that involves a variety of protein- and lipid-based remodeling events.
source: Transfer of cargo from EEs to LYs depends on an endosomal maturation process that involves a variety of protein- and lipid-based remodeling events.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Endosomal maturation involves a small GTPase RAB5-to-RAB7 switch.
source: They include a small GTPase RAB5-to-RAB7 switch, a PtdIns(3)P to PtdIns(3,5)P2 conversion, and changes in the luminal ion concentrations, most notably a decrease in pH (Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Endosomal maturation involves a PtdIns(3)P to PtdIns(3,5)P2 conversion.
source: They include a small GTPase RAB5-to-RAB7 switch, a PtdIns(3)P to PtdIns(3,5)P2 conversion, and changes in the luminal ion concentrations, most notably a decrease in pH (Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Endosomal maturation involves changes in the luminal ion concentrations, most notably a decrease in pH.
source: They include a small GTPase RAB5-to-RAB7 switch, a PtdIns(3)P to PtdIns(3,5)P2 conversion, and changes in the luminal ion concentrations, most notably a decrease in pH (Huotari and Helenius, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Endosome maturation involves sorting of membrane cargo destined for degradation into intraluminal vesicles (ILVs), thereby generating late endosomal vacuoles referred to as multivesicular bodies (MVBs).
source: Endosome maturation also involves sorting of membrane cargo destined for degradation into intraluminal vesicles (ILVs), thereby generating late endosomal vacuoles referred to as multivesicular bodies (MVBs) (Piper and Katzmann, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Ubiquitin has emerged as an important regulator of endocytosis and cargo degradation.
source: Ubiquitin has emerged as an important regulator of endocytosis and cargo degradation (Clague et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Ubiquitin serves as a signal for membrane quality control, endocytic internalization, endosome maturation, and cargo sorting into ILVs by the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs).
source: It serves as a signal for membrane quality control, endocytic internalization, endosome maturation, and cargo sorting into ILVs by the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRTs) (Piper et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Ubiquitination is indispensable for the interaction of EGFR with the ESCRT-0 complex member HRS and thus for efficient lysosomal targeting.
source: Indeed, ubiquitination is indispensable for the interaction of EGFR with the ESCRT-0 complex member HRS and thus for efficient lysosomal targeting (Eden et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Specific deubiquitination enzymes (DUBs) like AMSH and UBPY associate with ESCRT components to cleave and recycle ubiquitin.
source: Specific deubiquitination enzymes (DUBs) like AMSH and UBPY associate with ESCRT components to cleave and recycle ubiquitin (Alwan and van Leeuwen, 2007; Meijer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: In CUL3-depleted cells, late endosomes fail to mature properly.
source: In a recent study, we observed that Cullin-3 (CUL3) is involved in regulating endosome maturation and endo-lysosomal trafficking in mammalian cells. In CUL3-depleted cells, late endosomes fail to mature properly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referencing a previous study.

claim: In CUL3-depleted cells, late endosomes are enlarged and often devoid of ILVs.
source: They are enlarged and often devoid of ILVs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referencing a previous study.

claim: In CUL3-depleted cells, EGFR degradation is delayed and its ligand EGF accumulates in LE/LYs.
source: EGFR degradation is delayed and its ligand EGF accumulates in LE/LYs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referencing a previous study.

claim: CUL3-depleted cells are resistant to influenza A virus (IAV) infection because endocytosed virus particles remain associated with immature LE vacuoles instead of delivering their capsid components to the cytosol and the nucleus.
source: Moreover, the cells are resistant to influenza A virus (IAV) infection because instead of delivering their capsid components to the cytosol and the nucleus, the endocytosed virus particles remain associated with immature LE vacuoles (Huotari et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: CUL3 is the scaffolding subunit common for a large subfamily of Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases (CRLs).
source: CUL3 is the scaffolding subunit common for a large subfamily of Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) that mainly use the RING-H2 finger protein RBX1 to recruit charged ubiquitin conjugating enzymes (E2s) and catalyse the transfer of ubiquitin onto substrates (Lydeard et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: CRLs mainly use the RING-H2 finger protein RBX1 to recruit charged ubiquitin conjugating enzymes (E2s) and catalyse the transfer of ubiquitin onto substrates.
source: CUL3 is the scaffolding subunit common for a large subfamily of Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) that mainly use the RING-H2 finger protein RBX1 to recruit charged ubiquitin conjugating enzymes (E2s) and catalyse the transfer of ubiquitin onto substrates (Lydeard et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: CRL activity is stimulated by the conjugation of the ubiquitin-like protein NEDD8 to the cullin subunit.
source: This is stimulated by the conjugation of the ubiquitin-like protein NEDD8 to the cullin subunit (Duda et al., 2008; Saha and Deshaies, 2008) through an enzymatic cascade analogous to ubiquitination (Enchev et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CUL3 may be activated at endosomes by DCNL3, an E3 ligase for NEDD8, known to associate with membranes by virtue of a covalent lipid modification.
source: CUL3 may be activated at endosomes by DCNL3, an E3 ligase for NEDD8, known to associate with membranes by virtue of a covalent lipid modification (Meyer-Schaller et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: CRL activity is modulated by deneddylation as well as non-catalytically by the COP9 signalosome.
source: CRL activity is further modulated by deneddylation as well as non-catalytically by the COP9 signalosome (Emberley et al., 2012; Enchev et al., 2012; Fischer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: CRL3 complexes contain a subunit that binds to CUL3 through a Bric-a-brac/Tramtrack/Broad (BTB) domain.
source: In addition to CUL3, RBX1, and NEDD8, the CRL3 complexes contain a subunit that binds to CUL3 through a Bric-a-brac/Tramtrack/Broad (BTB) domain.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: BTB domain-containing proteins possess diverse substrate recognition domains and function as CRL3-specific substrate adaptors.
source: The BTB domain-containing proteins possess diverse substrate recognition domains and function as CRL3-specific substrate adaptors (Pintard et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: There are about 150 different BTB domain-containing proteins in the human proteome.
source: There are about 150 different BTB domain-containing proteins in the human proteome (Stogios et al., 2005), indicating that a large cohort of CRL3 substrates exists, most of which are presently unidentified.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Depletion of 14 BTB proteins caused 50% or greater decrease in the number of IAV infected cells.
source: Depletion of 14 BTB proteins caused 50% or greater decrease in the number of IAV infected cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening results.

claim: Depletion of SPOP or SPOPL gave a phenotype of defective virus uncoating similar to that observed after CUL3 depletion.
source: Out of 14 primary hits, we decided to follow up the BTB proteins SPOP and SPOPL because their depletion gave a phenotype of defective virus uncoating similar to that observed after CUL3 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Knockdown of SPOP or SPOPL resulted in a reduction of viral NP expression in A549 and HeLa cells to levels comparable to CUL3 depletion.
source: Knockdown of SPOP or SPOPL with the siRNAs resulted in a reduction of viral NP expression in A549 and HeLa cells to levels comparable to CUL3 depletion (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), but not as strong as upon depletion of a vATPase subunit (siATP6V1B2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cells depleted of either SPOP or SPOPL showed a block in IAV uncoating.
source: As expected, cells that were depleted of either SPOP or SPOPL showed a block in IAV uncoating (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: In SPOP or SPOPL-depleted cells, subsequent nuclear import of NP was impaired.
source: As a consequence, subsequent nuclear import of NP was also impaired (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Virus binding to the cell surface was elevated in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: Aside from virus binding to the cell surface, which was elevated in SPOPL-depleted cells, we found that endocytosis, acidification and fusion of the viral particles were comparable to controls (Figure 1C–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1C–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Endocytosis, acidification and fusion of the viral particles were comparable to controls in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: Aside from virus binding to the cell surface, which was elevated in SPOPL-depleted cells, we found that endocytosis, acidification and fusion of the viral particles were comparable to controls (Figure 1C–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1C–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: The defects in IAV uncoating and nuclear import of vRNPs in SPOP or SPOPL-depleted cells were rescued by a brief acidic incubation of virus bound to the cell surface.
source: The defects in IAV uncoating and nuclear import of vRNPs in SPOP or SPOPL-depleted cells were rescued by a brief acidic incubation of virus bound to the cell surface (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1H.

claim: GFP-tagged SPOP was predominantly nuclear when expressed in HeLa cells.
source: We found that while GFP-tagged SPOP was predominantly nuclear when expressed in HeLa cells, GFP-tagged SPOPL was cytoplasmic and confined to puncta (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: GFP-tagged SPOPL was cytoplasmic and confined to puncta when expressed in HeLa cells.
source: We found that while GFP-tagged SPOP was predominantly nuclear when expressed in HeLa cells, GFP-tagged SPOPL was cytoplasmic and confined to puncta (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Endogenous SPOPL, contrary to SPOP, was mainly in the soluble cytosolic fraction after sedimentation of total cell extracts prepared from HeLa cells.
source: Endogenous SPOPL, contrary to SPOP, was mainly in the soluble cytosolic fraction after sedimentation of total cell extracts prepared from HeLa cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Some of the SPOPL and CUL3 co-fractionated with endosomal markers such as EPS15, HRS and STAM in endosome purification.
source: Moreover, endosome purification revealed that some of the SPOPL and CUL3 co-fractionated with endosomal markers such as EPS15, HRS and STAM (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Early endosomes appeared normal in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to control siRNAs when visualized by the marker GFP-RAB5.
source: When visualized by the marker GFP-RAB5 using live cell imaging, early endosomes appeared normal in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to control siRNAs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: The late endosomal system as monitored by GFP-RAB7 was severely distorted when SPOPL was depleted.
source: In contrast, the late endosomal system as monitored by GFP-RAB7 was severely distorted when SPOPL was depleted by a siRNA or a shRNA construct (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The diameter of GFP-RAB7 positive endosomes increased two fold in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: The diameter of GFP-RAB7 positive endosomes increased two fold and the swollen vacuoles were clustered in the perinuclear region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: A similar defect to SPOPL depletion was observed when CRL activity was pharmacologically inhibited by the addition of MLN-4924.
source: A similar defect was observed when CRL activity was pharmacologically inhibited by the addition of MLN-4924 (Figure 2C), which prevents cullin neddylation (Soucy et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C with a citation.

claim: The endosome-to-Golgi transport marker GFP-RAB9 revealed strongly enlarged vacuoles upon SPOPL depletion.
source: Moreover, the endosome-to-Golgi transport marker GFP-RAB9 revealed strongly enlarged vacuoles upon SPOPL depletion as well, implying a broad effect of SPOPL on the late endosomal transport system (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Qualitative EM analysis of SPOPL-depleted cells showed that endosomal vacuoles were empty or contained little dense material and few ILVs were detectable compared to control cells.
source: Qualitative EM analysis of SPOPL-depleted cells showed that endosomal vacuoles were empty or contained little dense material and few ILVs were detectable compared to control cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: Depletion of SPOPL caused changes in late endocytic markers, in particular the MVB markers EPS15, HRS, STAM and TSG101.
source: In contrast to SPOP, depletion of SPOPL caused changes in late endocytic markers, in particular the MVB markers EPS15, HRS, STAM and TSG101.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The level of most early endocytic and recycling markers did not change upon SPOPL depletion.
source: The level of most early endocytic and recycling markers did not change (Clathrin, EPSIN1, Caveolin, Calnexin, RAB11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Out of the tested receptors, EGFR and MET revealed significant level changes upon SPOPL depletion, while levels of VEGFR, IGF1R and HER2 were not altered.
source: Notable, out of the tested receptors, EGFR and MET revealed significant level changes, while levels of VEGFR, IGF1R and HER2 - a close relative of EGFR - were not altered.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In contrast to the ESCRT components HRS and STAM and the endocytic adaptor EPS15, the lysosomal marker LAMP1 and early endocytic marker EEA1 were reduced in endosomal fractions upon SPOPL depletion.
source: Analysis of the endosome fraction revealed that in contrast to the ESCRT components HRS and STAM and the endocytic adaptor EPS15, the lysosomal marker LAMP1 and early endocytic marker EEA1 were reduced in endosomal fractions upon SPOPL depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: EGFR was strongly reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: Interestingly, we found that EGFR was strongly reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 3A), while it was elevated in cells depleted of CUL3 (Huotari et al., 2012) and in cells treated with the CRL-inhibitor MLN-4924 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: EGFR was elevated in cells depleted of CUL3.
source: Interestingly, we found that EGFR was strongly reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 3A), while it was elevated in cells depleted of CUL3 (Huotari et al., 2012) and in cells treated with the CRL-inhibitor MLN-4924 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EGFR was elevated in cells treated with the CRL-inhibitor MLN-4924.
source: Interestingly, we found that EGFR was strongly reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 3A), while it was elevated in cells depleted of CUL3 (Huotari et al., 2012) and in cells treated with the CRL-inhibitor MLN-4924 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Overexpression of HA-tagged SPOPL caused a two fold increase in EGFR and a 50% decrease in EPS15.
source: Conversely, overexpression of HA-tagged SPOPL caused a two fold increase in EGFR and a 50% decrease in EPS15 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: EPS15 accumulation observed in SPOPL-depleted cells was not associated with increased EPS15 mRNA.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR revealed that EPS15 accumulation observed in SPOPL-depleted cells was not associated with increased EPS15 mRNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: GFP-tagged EPS15 expressed from the doxycycline (Dox)-inducible promoter was elevated at least five fold in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to RNAi-controls.
source: Moreover, GFP-tagged EPS15 expressed from the doxycycline (Dox)-inducible promoter was elevated at least five fold in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to RNAi-controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GFP-EPS15 was stabilized upon MG132 addition in a concentration-dependent manner, but not by chloroquine.
source: GFP-EPS15 was stabilized upon MG132 addition in a concentration-dependent manner, but not by chloroquine.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: EPS15 is degraded by the proteasome.
source: Similarly, endogenous EPS15 levels slightly increased with increasing MG132 concentrations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), indicating that EPS15 is degraded by the proteasome.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Immunofluorescence microscopy showed SPOPL-GFP in vesicle-like structures that partially overlapped with EPS15 and EGFR.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy showed SPOPL-GFP in vesicle-like structures that partially overlapped with EPS15 and EGFR (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: SPOPL-GFP partially co-localized with the early endosomes marker EEA1, while it was not detected in LAMP1-containing structures.
source: Moreover, SPOPL-GFP partially co-localized with the early endosomes marker EEA1, while it was not detected in LAMP1-containing structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Endogenous immunoprecipitation revealed that EPS15 precipitates with SPOPL but not with SPOP in cell extracts.
source: Consistent with this localization data, endogenous immunoprecipitation revealed that EPS15 precipitates with SPOPL but not with SPOP in cell extracts (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: Recombinant GST-tagged EPS15 was purified from E. coli and tested for its ability to bind to purified SPOPL, and SPOPL was eluted specifically with GST-EPS15 in vitro.
source: Furthermore, recombinant GST-tagged EPS15 was purified from E. coli and tested for its ability to bind to purified SPOPL. SPOPL was eluted specifically with GST-EPS15 in vitro (Figure 3F), demonstrating direct association of the two proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F.

claim: EPS15 was readily ubiquitinated in a SPOPL-dependent manner in vitro.
source: As shown in Figure 3G, EPS15 was readily ubiquitinated in a SPOPL-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3G.

claim: Depending on the E2 enzyme - UBE2R1 (CDC34) or UBE2D1 (UBCH5) - EPS15 was poly-, mono- and di-ubiquitinated, respectively.
source: Depending on the E2 enzyme - UBE2R1 (CDC34) or UBE2D1 (UBCH5) - EPS15 was poly-, mono- and di-ubiquitinated, respectively (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: EPS15 is ubiquitinated in a CRL3SPOPL-dependent manner in vitro and ubiquitination leads to its proteasomal degradation.
source: These results demonstrated that EPS15 is ubiquitinated in a CRL3SPOPL-dependent manner in vitro and that ubiquitination leads to its proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: EPS15 contains two ubiquitin-interacting motifs (UIM) in its C-terminal domain that serve as a hub for regulation via ubiquitination in vivo.
source: EPS15 contains two ubiquitin-interacting motifs (UIM) in its C-terminal domain that serve as a hub for regulation via ubiquitination in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The EPS15 amino acid sequence predicts SPOP binding motifs (Φ-π-S-S/T-S/T, Φ = nonpolar, π = polar).
source: Moreover, the EPS15 amino acid sequence predicts SPOP binding motifs (Φ-π-S-S/T-S/T, Φ = nonpolar, π = polar) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Zhuang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and supported by Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ubiquitination of K793 in EPS15, located in the C-terminal domain close to the ubiquitin-interacting motifs (UIMs), was significantly reduced in cells lacking SPOPL.
source: In contrast, ubiquitination of K793, located in the C-terminal domain of EPS15 close to the ubiquitin-interacting motifs (UIMs) (Figure 4A), was significantly reduced in cells lacking SPOPL.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: Binding of SPOPL to the EPS15S605-607A mutant was comparable to wild-type controls, while the ability of EPS15S744-746A to interact with SPOPL was severely reduced.
source: While binding of SPOPL to the EPS15S605-607A mutant was comparable to wild-type controls, the ability of EPS15S744-746A to interact with SPOPL was severely reduced (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C.

claim: SPOPL preferentially binds EPS15 through the conserved TSSSV motif.
source: This showed that SPOPL preferentially binds EPS15 through the conserved TSSSV motif.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The steady-state levels of EPS15S744-746A-GFP were increased at least six fold, concomitant with decreased EGFR levels.
source: Indeed, the steady-state levels of EPS15S744-746A-GFP were increased at least six fold, concomitant with decreased EGFR levels, and no further increase of EPS15S744-746A-GFP levels was detected by simultaneously depleting SPOPL (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: No further increase of EPS15S744-746A-GFP levels was detected by simultaneously depleting SPOPL.
source: Indeed, the steady-state levels of EPS15S744-746A-GFP were increased at least six fold, concomitant with decreased EGFR levels, and no further increase of EPS15S744-746A-GFP levels was detected by simultaneously depleting SPOPL (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: The lysine 793 is relevant for EPS15 turnover via CRL3SPOPL in cells.
source: Although it showed reduced expression, when compared to wild type, no stabilization was detected after SPOPL depletion, suggesting that the lysine 793 is indeed relevant for EPS15 turnover via CRL3SPOPL in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: When HA-tagged SPOPL was overexpressed, degradation of the binding mutant EPS15S744-746A-GFP and the SPOPL-ubiquitination-deficient mutant EPS15K793R-GFP were not induced in contrast to wild-type EPS15.
source: Furthermore, when HA-tagged SPOPL was overexpressed, degradation of the binding mutant EPS15S744-746A-GFP and the SPOPL-ubiquitination-deficient mutant EPS15K793R-GFP were not induced in contrast to wild-type EPS15 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: CRL3SPOPL binds to a conserved SPOP/SPOPL binding motif in EPS15 and ubiquitinates EPS15 on lysine K793, which results in proteasomal degradation of EPS15.
source: We concluded that CRL3SPOPL binds to a conserved SPOP/SPOPL binding motif in EPS15. It ubiquitinates EPS15 on lysine K793, which evidently results in proteasomal degradation of EPS15.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: EGFR was more rapidly degraded after addition of EGF in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to RNAi-controls.
source: We found that EGFR was more rapidly degraded after addition of EGF in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to RNAi-controls, while its internalization judging by EGFR ubiquitination and EGF uptake was similar (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EGFR internalization judging by EGFR ubiquitination and EGF uptake was similar in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to controls.
source: We found that EGFR was more rapidly degraded after addition of EGF in SPOPL-depleted cells compared to RNAi-controls, while its internalization judging by EGFR ubiquitination and EGF uptake was similar (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The degradation of EGFR in SPOPL-depleted cells was blocked by chloroquine, which inhibits the acidification of endosomes and LYs, confirming that EGFR was degraded in lysosomes.
source: The degradation was blocked by chloroquine, which inhibits the acidification of endosomes and LYs (Figure 5B), confirming that EGFR was degraded in lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Overexpression of EPS15-GFP only decreased the EGFR levels in the absence of SPOPL.
source: Overexpression of EPS15-GFP only decreased the EGFR levels in the absence of SPOPL (Figure 5C), implying that EPS15 accumulation alone may not be sufficient to promote EGFR degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: EGFR levels increased in cells lacking both SPOPL and EPS15, demonstrating that EPS15 is necessary to promote EGFR degradation in the absence of SPOPL.
source: Indeed, EGFR levels increased in cells lacking both SPOPL and EPS15, demonstrating that EPS15 is necessary to promote EGFR degradation in the absence of SPOPL (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: EPS15 at the plasma membrane was unaffected by SPOPL depletion.
source: While EPS15 at the plasma membrane was unaffected by SPOPL depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), EPS15 accumulated in intracellular structures upon SPOPL-depletion and increasingly co-localized with the ESCRT-0 subunit HRS (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: EPS15 accumulated in intracellular structures upon SPOPL-depletion and increasingly co-localized with the ESCRT-0 subunit HRS.
source: While EPS15 at the plasma membrane was unaffected by SPOPL depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), EPS15 accumulated in intracellular structures upon SPOPL-depletion and increasingly co-localized with the ESCRT-0 subunit HRS (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The interaction of EPS15 and EGFR is reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: Indeed, the interaction of EPS15 and EGFR is reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), while the interaction of EPS15 and HRS is stabilized (Figure 5F), consistent with the idea that EPS15 ubiquitination promotes EGFR stabilization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The interaction of EPS15 and HRS is stabilized in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: Indeed, the interaction of EPS15 and EGFR is reduced in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), while the interaction of EPS15 and HRS is stabilized (Figure 5F), consistent with the idea that EPS15 ubiquitination promotes EGFR stabilization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5F.

claim: Loss of SPOPL-mediated ubiquitination of EPS15 favors EGFR sorting and trafficking into the lysosomal pathway via HRS.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that loss of SPOPL-mediated ubiquitination of EPS15 favors EGFR sorting and trafficking into the lysosomal pathway via HRS (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data and supported by Figure 6.

claim: EPS15 was originally identified as a substrate for the EGFR kinase that interacts with the clathrin assembly adaptors AP2 and EPSIN1.
source: EPS15 was originally identified as a substrate for the EGFR kinase that interacts with the clathrin assembly adaptors AP2 and EPSIN1 (Benmerah et al., 1995; Chen et al., 1998; Fazioli et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: Perturbation of EPS15 and EPSIN1 function blocks endocytosis of EGF and transferrin, demonstrating that they are part of the primary endocytic machinery at the plasma membrane.
source: Perturbation of EPS15 and EPSIN1 function blocks endocytosis of EGF and transferrin, demonstrating that they are part of the primary endocytic machinery at the plasma membrane (Carbone et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: EPS15 promotes vesicular trafficking intracellularly.
source: In addition, EPS15 promotes vesicular trafficking intracellularly (Yuan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: Overexpression of shorter isoforms (EPS15S, EPS15B) determines cargo recycling or degradation at endosomes.
source: Overexpression of shorter isoforms (EPS15S, EPS15B) determines cargo recycling or degradation at endosomes (Chi et al., 2011; Roxrud et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: EPS15 is known to associate with the E3-ligases NEDD4 and Parkin (PARK2) and is mono-ubiquitinated by them.
source: EPS15 is moreover known to associate with the E3-ligases NEDD4 and Parkin (PARK2) and is mono-ubiquitinated by them (Fallon et al., 2006; Polo et al., 2002; Woelk et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: A single ubiquitin in the C-terminal domain reduces binding of EPS15 to free ubiquitin thus impairing association with ubiquitinated client proteins and co-localization with EGFR on endosomes.
source: For example, a single ubiquitin in the C-terminal domain reduces binding of EPS15 to free ubiquitin thus impairing association with ubiquitinated client proteins and co-localization with EGFR on endosomes (Hoeller et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: Ubiquitination by the CRL3SPOPL complex inhibits EPS15 function in endosome maturation.
source: Our own data shows that ubiquitination by the CRL3SPOPL complex inhibits EPS15 function in endosome maturation (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data and supported by Figure 6.

claim: EPS15 forms a trimeric complex with the ESCRT components HRS and STAM and interacts with EGFR and HRS 30 min after EGF uptake.
source: EPS15 forms a trimeric complex with the ESCRT components HRS and STAM and interacts with EGFR and HRS 30 min after EGF uptake (Bache, 2003; Sigismund et al., 2005)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: Upon HRS depletion, EPS15 accumulates on endosomes.
source: Upon HRS depletion, EPS15 accumulates on endosomes (Gucwa and Brown, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: SPOPL depletion promotes endosomal co-localization of EPS15 with HRS.
source: Our results showed that SPOPL depletion promotes endosomal co-localization of EPS15 with HRS.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: EPS15 association with HRS is important for EPS15 turnover and for targeting of the EGFR to lysosomes for degradation.
source: This implies that EPS15 association with HRS is important for EPS15 turnover and for targeting of the EGFR to lysosomes for degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: A change in the phosphorylation state of EPS15 - either due to the mutation EPS15-Y850F or overexpression of the phosphatase PTPN3 – results in faster degradation of EGFR.
source: A change in the phosphorylation state of EPS15 - either due to the mutation EPS15-Y850F or overexpression of the phosphatase PTPN3 – results in faster degradation of EGFR (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: Upon SPOPL depletion EPS15 accumulates on HRS-containing vesicles and EGFR degradation is accelerated.
source: Because upon SPOPL depletion EPS15 accumulates on HRS-containing vesicles and EGFR degradation is accelerated, we propose that the EPS15-HRS complexes actively promote sorting of EPS15 clients such as the EGFR and MET to lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The EPS15-HRS complexes actively promote sorting of EPS15 clients such as the EGFR and MET to lysosomes.
source: Because upon SPOPL depletion EPS15 accumulates on HRS-containing vesicles and EGFR degradation is accelerated, we propose that the EPS15-HRS complexes actively promote sorting of EPS15 clients such as the EGFR and MET to lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposal based on the data.

claim: The depletion of USP9X leads to slower degradation of EGFR.
source: Interestingly, recent findings further demonstrate that EPS15 de-ubiquitination by USP9X affects EGFR internalization and its trafficking to lysosomes (Savio et al., 2016). In contrast to SPOPL depletion, the depletion of USP9X leads to slower degradation of EGFR.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: A cycle of ubiquitination / de-ubiquitination of EPS15 not only regulates the internalization pathway, but is also involved in the sorting of cargo in LEs.
source: Therefore, it is evident that a cycle of ubiquitination / de-ubiquitination of EPS15 not only regulates the internalization pathway, but is also involved in the sorting of cargo in LEs (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion and supported by Figure 6.

claim: ILV formation is a dynamic and tightly regulated process that involves recycling of the ESCRT components by VPS4.
source: Indeed, ILV formation is a dynamic and tightly regulated process that involves recycling of the ESCRT components by VPS4 (Babst et al., 1998; Sachse, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: ILV formation depends on SPOPL.
source: It is evident that ILV formation depends on SPOPL, and that loss of available ESCRT complexes due to loss of CRL3SPOPL activity prevents the reduction in the surface area of the endosomal limiting membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Loss of available ESCRT complexes due to loss of CRL3SPOPL activity prevents the reduction in the surface area of the endosomal limiting membrane.
source: It is evident that ILV formation depends on SPOPL, and that loss of available ESCRT complexes due to loss of CRL3SPOPL activity prevents the reduction in the surface area of the endosomal limiting membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The inhibition of IAV entry after SPOPL-depletion was similar to observations with CUL3-depletion.
source: The inhibition of IAV entry after SPOPL-depletion was similar to our previous observations with CUL3-depletion (Huotari et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: IAV was endocytosed normally and reached a late endosomal compartment acidic enough to induce HA-conversion and membrane fusion/hemifusion in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: This late penetrating virus was endocytosed normally and reached a late endosomal compartment acidic enough to induce HA-conversion and membrane fusion/hemifusion.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion.

claim: The uncoating process that involves dissociation of the matrix protein M1 shell and release of the vRNPs from the endosome did not take place in SPOPL-depleted cells.
source: However, the uncoating process that involves dissociation of the matrix protein M1 shell and release of the vRNPs from the endosome did not take place.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion.

claim: Uncoating of IAV capsids requires priming of the viral capsid prior to fusion by exposure to low pH and potassium ions in the lumen of endosomes as well as the function of the ubiquitin-vacuolar protein sorting system and interaction with a number of host cell factors in the cytosol.
source: Recent studies have indicated that uncoating of IAV capsids is a complex process that requires priming of the viral capsid prior to fusion by exposure to low pH and potassium ions in the lumen of endosomes as well as the function of the ubiquitin-vacuolar protein sorting system and interaction with a number of host cell factors in the cytosol (Banerjee et al., 2014; Khor et al., 2003; Martin and Helenius, 1991; Stauffer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations.

claim: EGFR signaling is required for efficient IAV infection.
source: Moreover, the EGFR level could be crucial for IAV entry, since EGFR signaling is required for efficient IAV infection.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion.

claim: Virus binding leads to lipid-raft clustering, which activates EGFR and other RTKs and facilitates IAV uptake.
source: Available evidence suggests that virus binding leads to lipid-raft clustering, which activates EGFR and other RTKs and facilitates IAV uptake (Eierhoff et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: SPOP and SPOPL mainly differ by a 18 amino-acid insertion in SPOPL that may be responsible for their distinct subcellular localization.
source: SPOP and SPOPL mainly differ by a 18 amino-acid insertion in SPOPL (Errington et al., 2012) that may be responsible for their distinct subcellular localization, which likely underlies the observed substrate specificity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: SPOP and SPOPL have been shown to form heterodimers.
source: SPOP and SPOPL have also been shown to form heterodimers, and in vitro experiments have suggested that SPOPL may inhibit SPOP activity by attenuating self assembly in a dose-dependent manner (Errington et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: In vitro experiments have suggested that SPOPL may inhibit SPOP activity by attenuating self assembly in a dose-dependent manner.
source: SPOP and SPOPL have also been shown to form heterodimers, and in vitro experiments have suggested that SPOPL may inhibit SPOP activity by attenuating self assembly in a dose-dependent manner (Errington et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation.

claim: It is likely that SPOPL regulates additional substrates at endosomes.
source: While we could demonstrate that CRL3SPOPL directly ubiquitinates EPS15, it is likely that SPOPL regulates additional substrates at endosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation.

claim: CRL3SPOPL may directly or indirectly affect ESCRT components STAM and HRS.
source: That EPS15, STAM, and to a lesser extent HRS levels were increased in SPOPL-depleted cells (Figure 2E) raises the possibility that CRL3SPOPL directly or indirectly affects these ESCRT components.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: CUL3 must modify additional targets relevant for endocytic trafficking.
source: Finally, it is clear that CUL3 must modify additional targets relevant for endocytic trafficking.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion.

claim: Downregulation of SPOPL decreases EGFR levels, whereas CUL3-depletion results in greatly elevated levels of EGFR.
source: Indeed, downregulation of SPOPL decreases EGFR levels, whereas CUL3-depletion results in greatly elevated levels of EGFR, most likely due to a reduced ability of endosomes to fuse with lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion.
